advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a producer-liveness anchor to integration AC1 (assert `peer_sync.returncode == 0` and/or assert a PRESENCE log line proving reconverge reached the lock-wait region) before trusting the warning-absence check.
evidence: peer_sync is run with `check=False` and its `.returncode` is never asserted before the absence check (tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py:977-989)

The fixed path is a silent return: sync.py:342-343 `except _lock.LockTimeout:` / `return` — no log emitted, so a correctly-waiting reconverge produces the SAME empty stdout as one that returned early at sync.py:293/304/320/324
The preceding precondition asserts (MERGE_HEAD present, write_lock_is_busy, pid match at lines 967-970) verify the PUSH process, not the peer_sync producer whose stdout the oracle reads

The Capture logging handler is configured at DEBUG level (_DRAKE_SYNC_CODE `logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)`), so an asserted PRESENCE line from the same capture is feasible as a liveness anchor but is not used
advisory.finding: Integration test AC1 asserts absence of the `fsck-recover` pre-lock warning from the peer_sync subprocess's stdout with no producer-liveness anchor. Because sync.reconverge has several early returns before the lock-wait region (os.path.isdir at sync.py:292, ConfigError at 302-304, _coordinated_fetch failure at 319-320, rev-parse --verify at 323-324) and the fixed lock-timeout path returns silently (sync.py:342-343), the absence check passes both when the fix works AND when reconverge never reached the region under test — it cannot distinguish its verdict from the producer never running.
scenarios: A future change makes reconverge return early during config resolution or fetch on the peer's tracker; AC1 stays green while never exercising the pre-lock-vs-lock-wait behavior the test exists to protect.
advisory.suggested_fix: Before the `assert not _drake_reconverge_warned_at_pre_lock_site(...)` line, assert the peer reconverge actually ran the region under test — e.g. `assert peer_sync.returncode == 0, peer_sync.stderr` plus an asserted PRESENCE of a fetch/lock-wait DEBUG record from the same stdout capture (add such a log line to reconverge's lock-wait/timeout path if none exists), so the absence check can no longer pass when reconverge returned early.

coaching.coaching: File a follow-on ticket (discovered_from this change) for missing producer-liveness anchor in AC1 assertion, a pre-existing / out-of-scope issue — do not fix it in this change.
coaching.subject: missing producer-liveness anchor in AC1 assertion
